name: Preserve food
summary: Drying, salting, smoking, pickling and canning all work without power; cold storage needs the most. Salt is the overlooked staple: restaurants and food warehouses hold sacks of it, and it never goes off. Dry goods sealed in food-grade buckets, kept cool and dark, last for years.

parts.why: Cures meat and fish, and brines vegetables
Food-grade buckets and drums keep stores dry and pest-free
Keeps cured and fresh food cool
Lines a root cellar or cold box

tips: Low-acid foods (meat, beans, most vegetables) must be pressure-canned. Boiling-water canning is safe only for acidic foods like fruit, jam and pickles.
Use food salt where you can. Water softener and road salt aren’t made for food; road salt holds grit and chemicals.
Cool, dark and dry storage makes any food last far longer.
Bulging cans, spurting lids or a bad smell mean throw it out. Never taste to check.
